rows.name: SEPIA
rows.reason: SEPIA provides self-hosted assistance, clients and extensible NLU. Local backend does not ensure local speech recognition; maintenance, recognition quality and language/hardware fit remain unestablished. No survival guarantee.

rows.name: Home Assistant Assist with a local voice pipeline
rows.reason: Local speech/intent/response pipeline adds home-automation voice control; requires audio hardware and configured actions. April 2023 evidence does not establish an option for the July 2021 question.

rows.name: Kalliope
rows.reason: Kalliope offers modular Linux/Raspberry Pi assistance. Default speech recognition is Google; self-hosting alone does not keep speech local. Select CMUSphinx/local TTS and verify compatibility.

rows.name: SEPIA Framework
rows.reason: SEPIA offers self-hosted assistance, NLU, reminders, browser/mobile clients and extensible device control. Core hosting does not establish offline speech engines or third-party services; administration work remains.

rows.name: Leon
rows.reason: Leon is relevant self-hostable assistance, but current unfinished 2.0 preview does not verify legacy voice deployment. Legacy retrieval failed; voice readiness, speech dependencies and suitable stable version remain unverified.

rows.name: Mycroft / Mycroft Core
rows.reason: Mycroft Core repeats the referenced assistant rather than supplying an alternative. Later maintenance-end and 2024 archival notices are caveats, not mandatory exclusions or evidence available in July 2021.

rows.name: Kalliope
rows.reason: Locally hosted voice-action framework requires composing behavior. Default recognizer is Google; local STT is optional, not automatic. Commands, language support, installation success and ongoing maintenance untested.

rows.name: Rhasspy Voice Assistant
rows.reason: Offline DIY voice pipeline requires commands and intent-action handlers. 2025 archival remains a longevity caveat, but no hard maintenance threshold in the summary mandates exclusion.

rows.name: Rhasspy
rows.reason: Offline DIY intent toolkit requires user-authored commands/actions. Repository archived 2025-10-06, limiting current longevity; later archival does not establish what was knowable in 2021.

rows.name: Rhino 3D
rows.reason: Rhino's 3D modeling/design role mismatches a self-hosted voice assistant; no concrete transfer established. Exclusion does not rely on unmentioned features or license preferences.

rows.name: Jasper
rows.reason: Open-source platform for always-on voice applications and custom modules on ordinary hardware. Homepage establishes design, but not current maintenance, modern dependency compatibility or complete offline operation.

rows.name: OpenVoiceOS
rows.reason: Offline-capable open-source assistant uses separate listening/intent/audio/messaging components. Current guidance is undated relative to question, and distributions can lag; no ready July 2021 replacement is established.

rows.name: Mycroft / Mycroft Core
rows.reason: It is the already-considered assistant whose continuity prompted the question; keeping the same core does not provide an independently maintained alternative.

rows.name: Rhasspy
rows.reason: Offline voice interface maps commands to self-hosted Home Assistant/Node-RED actions. Requires command authoring and intent handlers; no turnkey Alexa equivalence established. Current repository reports October 2025 archival.

rows.name: Rhino 3D
rows.reason: Rhino 3D is geometry modeling and design software; the supplied product provides neither a voice-assistant platform nor the speech components needed here.

rows.name: Rhasspy Voice Assistant
rows.reason: Its offline speech services produce intent events for Home Assistant or Node-RED, directly supporting a customizable self-hosted alternative to Mycroft.

rows.name: Leon
rows.reason: Open-source self-hosted assistant supports personalized automation. Current default branch is an unfinished 2.0 rewrite; previous version is on master. Preview documentation cannot establish a stable 2021 product.
